A rack of pork ribs prepared as follows:

  1. Remove the membrane and coat with "rib rub"
  2. Wrap with plastic and leave in the fridge for 24 hours
  3. Put on the grill at 250 F for three hours (flip at 1.5 hours)
  4. Coat in BBQ sauce and turn the heat up to high, cook just long enough to caramelize the sauce (5min top)

Enjoy with a Fat Tire.
Another tip for new grillers is to put a pan of water under the meat in order to keep the meat moist and not dry, nobody likes dry meat.
Or a pan of beans under the ribs to catch the drippings. So good.

The simplest and cheap meal that is very delicious is this dish called SOS my dad made, basically ground beef and a roux/gravy on toast with Worcestershire sauce. My dad's dad was in the air force, it was taught to my grandfather there. You brown the ground beef in a skillet (with some salt and pepper), and then add flour and milk, and reduce the mixture until it is the consistency of gravy or slightly thinner depending on how thick you like it. You can add some onions and mushrooms when you are browning the meat for more flavor, or sausage instead of beef for the morning. You only use one dish, and only ingredients you probably already have and can prepare easily. here are some recipes for exact amounts and more thorough instructions; http://www.food.com/recipe/sos-stuff-on-a-shingle-130886, http://www.food.com/recipe/sausage-or-beef-s-o-s-stuff-on-a-shingle-152508, http://www.food.com/recipe/sos-stuff-on-a-shingle-130886.
